messages.subject: Re: Updating Renjin's Database packages
messages.body_plain:
Dear Alex,

Le jeudi 29 décembre 2016 12:39:28 UTC+1, Alexander Bertram a écrit :

> Hi Erwan,

> I think it is possible, but I think it would probably require getting a version of rjdbc working well on Renjin so that there could be a common starting point. I don't think that's too far off, as Parham's work on the renjin-jdbc library probably provides most of the implementation:
> https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-jdbc
>
> You will also probably need some build script magic to deal with the JAR dependencies: Renjin expects them to be declared in the package's pom file while rJava expects to find them bundled with the package sources.
>
> I need to take a look at where we are in general with this migration effort and can share an update in the new year.

Thanks. Indeed It will be very nice to offer a mechanism (if it's possible) to contribute to the R community.

Once again thanks a lot for this great library.

Erwan

>
> Best,
> Alex
>
>
> On Thu, Dec 22, 2016 at 1:41 PM Erwan Bocher <erwan....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Dear Alex,
> >
> > Thank for the advices and thanks a lot of for your excellent job.
> > Do you think it possible, reliable to create a RH2GIS package available both for R (CRAN) and Rengin ?
> > Best regards
> >
> >
> >
> >
> >
> > Le lundi 7 novembre 2016 21:10:48 UTC+1, Alexander Bertram a écrit :
> > >
> > > Hi Erwan,
> > >
> > >
> > > There's no reason you can't continue to use the renjin-dbi project, as long as you specify the version.
> > >
> > > We won't be changing the renjin-dbi repo, so you can continue to build on that project.
> > >
> > > Best,
> > > Alex
> > >
> > > On Mon, Nov 7, 2016, 3:54 PM Erwan Bocher <erwan....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Dear Alex,
> > > >
> > > > After a quick check on S4 approach, I will not have time to transpose RH2GIS. It requiers a bit more time than the S3 approach that is easy to use and understand thanks to Hannes.
> > > > At the moment, I decided to use the Hannes's code.
> > > > Nevertheless, I have a question. Do I need to extract the RH2GIS code fron renjin-dbi repository because It will be replaced by the S4 module ?
> > > > If yes, how to get RH2GIS available for the Renjin community ? I think about the library resolver system.
> > > >
> > > > Best regards
> > > >
> > > > Erwan
> > > >
> > > > Le jeudi 20 octobre 2016 21:11:13 UTC+2, Alexander Bertram a écrit :
> > > > > Hi Erwan,
> > > > > What we have started to do is move all the core Java glue code from the DBI package to a new library "renjin-jdbc" that can be referenced by the separate database modules:
> > > > > https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-jdbc
> > > > >
> > > > > I would suggest creating a new repo for the RH2 and RH2GIS modules. The RH2 module contains a good template for defining the S4 classes required for DBI:
> > > > > https://github.com/dmkaplan2000/RH2/blob/master/R/class.R <https://www.google.com/url?q=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fdmkaplan2000%2FRH2%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2FR%2Fclass.R&sa=D&sntz=1&usg=AFQjCNHOZKaMqt728lHu3iCz_rDsLDFh8w>
> > > > >
> > > > > Just substitute JDBCDriver for DBIDriver, etc, and replace the rJava calls with calls to JDBCUtils$methodXXX()
> > > > >
> > > > > Parham is working on the RSQLite module, which might also provide some pointers:
> > > > > https://github.com/bedatadriven/RSQLite
> > > > >
> > > > > Best,
> > > > > Alex
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > On Thu, Oct 20, 2016 at 8:19 PM Erwan Bocher <erwan....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > Dear Alex,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Thank you for telling us about these information.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > RH2GIS is used by our software OrbisGIS. Without RH2GIS we are not able to manage R script between Renjin and our database.
> > > > > > As I wrote in https://github.com/hannesmuehleisen/renjin-dbi/issues/10, we want to improve DBI and support some features like custom table types or geometry type...
> > > > > > Because H2 and H2GIS are java based with have two options :
> > > > > >  - reorganize renjin-dbi to support only the database unsupported by S4-based DB,
> > > > > >  - align H2 and H2GIS with the official R package https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RH2/index.htm
> > > > > >
> > > > > > The second option is a bit ugly because of RJDBC, rJava dependencies.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Any comment and proposal are welcome.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Best regards
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Erwan
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Le lundi 17 octobre 2016 15:16:04 UTC+2, Alexander Bertram a écrit :
> > > > > > > Hi all,
> > > > > > > A while back, Hannes Mulheisen put together Renjin-specific versions of R's database packages, like DBI, RMySQL, MonetDB.R, etc:
> > > > > > > https://github.com/hannesmuehleisen/renjin-dbi <https://www.google.com/url?q=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fhannesmuehleisen%2Frenjin-dbi&sa=D&sntz=1&usg=AFQjCNFNhP0QZC1nE5svvUAsAhBq_0PSPQ>
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Since Renjin didn't support S4 very well at the time, Hannes wrote the new packages using S3, which provided basically the same syntax to the end user. Since then, the OrbisGIS group has done some great work on the drivers for H2 and H2GIS.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > However, as we are working to improve compatibility with the BioConductor packages, we've run into several cases where packages expect formal S4 classes like DBIConnection.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Over the next week or two, we'd like to start building the DBI package directly from source as-is, and then release forked versions of RSqlite and RMySQL that just swap out the C bits with a light java wrapper that calls out to JDBC.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > This will not only ensure greater interoperability with BioConductor packages, but will help keep these packages in sync with developments to RMySQL and RSqlite etc involve more database-specific functionality like escaping, etc, that our versions don't.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > As we make these changes, you can continue to use the versions of RH2 and RH2GIS that are based on Hannes' DBI, but you will need to be careful about transitive dependency conflicts for the next week or two: For example, the following may lead to tears:
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > library(RH2)  # loads the S3-based RH2 and DBI, so far so good
> > > > > > > library(RSQLite) # loads the latest version of RSQLite that expects the new S4-based DBI, fail.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Sorry for the inconvenience, and let us know if you can help with testing these new versions or if you're critically relying on some specific, current behavior.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > > Alex
> > > > > > >
> > > > > >

messages.subject: Join classloader
messages.body_plain:
Dear Alex,

We are using RenjinScriptEngineFactory into OrbisGIS to offer a swing console.
Currently, we populate a SessionBuilder based on the AetherPackageLoader in order to solve the library dependencies. Only one classloader (AetherPackageLoader.getClassLoader()) is loaded.
Consequently we are not able to access to the OrbisGIS objects because OrbisGIS uses its own classloader.
So my question
Is there a way or some advices to manage with Renjin two classloaders ?

Best regards.

messages.subject: Re: Join classloader
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erwan,

I've expanded the SessionBuilder and AetherPackageLoader APIs in 0.8.2310 to allow you to provide a parent class loader both to the AetherPackageLoader instance, and to the Session itself, which will be used to load classes referenced in ad hoc 'import(com.acme.MyClass)` calls.

I've also added a section to the documentation covering the customization of the runtime context that I hope will also be helpful:
http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/library/execution-context.html

Would much appreciate any comments or feedback on this section as you have experience actually using it. You can edit the doc directly here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-docs/blob/master/source/library/execution-context.rst

Best,
Alex

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to call R from Java.  In R Script we have used R library "RQuantLib",

library("RQuantLib")

So I have added corresponding maven dependency for this in my pom.

<dependency>
    <groupId>org.renjin.cran</groupId>
    <artifactId>RQuantLib</artifactId>
    <version>0.4.2-b30</version>
</dependency>

But I am struck with below error while execution.

Exception in thread "main" org.renjin.eval.EvalException: error in load action .__A__.1 for package RQuantLib: NULL: Could not load JVM class 'org.renjin.cran.RQuantLib.RQuantLib' from package 'org.renjin.cran.RQuantLib.RQuantLib'

I couldn't get much information about this error in web.  So it would be great if you provide some help on this.

Thanks for your help in advance.

Thanks & Regards,
Karthik B

messages.subject: Re: Reg : Error in RQuantLib
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karthik,

it looks like the RQuantlLib cannot be used in Renjin as the build system wasn't able to compile the sources to Java bytecode. You can see the same error message in one of the examples here: http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/RQuantLib/0.4.2/build/30#test-AmericanOption-examples

It seems that this package interfaces with QuantLib, which is a C++ library. The build system doesn't have this library installed and, even if it did, it will not be able to transpile this to Java bytecode. The same holds for other packages which depend on C libraries (e.g. libcurl, libxml, GNU scientific library, etc.) and our usual approach is to create "replacement" packages for these. This means that you would look for equivalent functionality in a Java library, but QuantLib seems very specific and this option is probably less obvious.

Maarten-Jan
